body:
Register a pinned public review dataset and inspect its observations in the local harness. The importer verifies source bytes, preserves every source record in immutable Parquet, and atomically records SQLite metadata and an event. The read-only browser queries through DuckDB and exposes source provenance and bounded pagination.

The semantic commits are arranged by capability:

1. [Register pinned source evidence](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/2c4f5bb5840a73cc694b16760459277d01529007).
2. [Browse registered observations](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/63246f01fb745c1cba887b32e0e0d6f8929b632a).
3. [Report typed architecture snapshots and deltas](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/b6fa32204d4b0a1f8e55bd2cbcafac2950037668).
4. [Backfill the existing quality runner's comments](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/dd12b4aa33c8271130d5729cb8914ecd99dc0fb4).
5. [Record the commenting convention, ADR-0003 and ADR lifecycle guidance](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/544dcf217a8b361bc7de3e98d5c68201f1f1e2d6).
6. [Record the owner's source-preservation decision in ADR-0002](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/commit/c66dcfe605e00a8b3ea41208647df11bb7be4da6).

Comments for new code accompany its introducing capability. ADR-0002 and ADR-0003 are implemented in this candidate; ADR-0001 remains accepted pending its first applicable empirical decision.

Validation: every exact checkpoint passed `uv run --locked python tools/check.py` in its own locked Windows/Python 3.12 environment: Ruff formatting/lint, Import Linter, Tach and 11/14/15/15/15/15 tests. The pinned 1,030-record public sample was imported and reopened during r3; those original results remain identified as r3 evidence. R4 changes documentation only: executable Python structure, tests, dependencies and typed architecture are unchanged. FastAPI handler docstrings also populate API descriptions.

DER r4: [retained histories, checkpoint logs, range-diff and self-review](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/tree/cded52fffec05bbfa2b10ec41c917d0e975d67dc). Frozen diary `797d8189ff7194bf025885ab0815b3f301fa21d2` and semantic tip `c66dcfe605e00a8b3ea41208647df11bb7be4da6` have exactly equal tracked trees. Earlier failed checks and their corrections are retained. This is self-review; no hosted CI checks are configured.

This is the first VS1 batch. Worker execution, llama.cpp/model routing, MAF normalisation and Accept/Edit/Reject annotation remain outstanding. PR approval and merge are for the owner; the evidence branch must not be merged into main.

comments.body: This seems quite broad - please break it down into smaller reviewable units - I'd like each capability in its own semantic commit as its introduced.

I would like to see code comments on module exposed methods, and on internal methods where the functionality implemented isn't obvious either in intent or implementation. Keep these brief and to the point. Let's discuss this in detail in the coding harness.

Agreed. I intend to add brief docstrings to the methods and functions exposed across module boundaries, and comments on internal logic where the intent or implementation is not obvious.

By coding harness, we mean the Codex conversation. We will discuss the convention there before I edit the code: what callers need to know for exposed interfaces, and the rationale or invariant behind non-obvious internal logic. The comments should stay concise and avoid restating the code.

Implemented the convention agreed in Codex in response to [your comment](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/pull/3#issuecomment-5744986964).

Concise docstrings now cover exposed operations, with comments explaining non-obvious publication, identity, transaction and architecture-inspection logic. These accompany their code in the three capability commits. The existing quality runner backfill has its own commit, and the guidance/ADR update is separate.

ADR-0003 is `implemented` after the backfill and passing checks. ADR-0002 is also `implemented` following your choice to preserve source records; ADR-0001 remains `accepted` pending first empirical use. ADR lifecycle checks are now explicit in the development guidance.

All six semantic checkpoints pass the canonical quality command, and the frozen diary and final semantic trees match exactly. [R4 evidence and previous histories](https://github.com/FinnNk/Meerkritic/tree/cded52fffec05bbfa2b10ec41c917d0e975d67dc) are retained. Current head: `c66dcfe605e00a8b3ea41208647df11bb7be4da6`. Owner review and merge remain outstanding.
